Rashi on Ketubot 60b:10:1.english: [If] she weaned him, [she is] prohibited - For she weaned him on account of wanting to marry.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:11:1.english: She stipulated a small [amount] - They stipulated to give her meager sustenance.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:11:2.hebrew: אוכלת הרבה - משלה, כדי שיהיה לה חלב הרבה ולא תמיתנו:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:11:2.english: She [must] eat much - From her own [means], so that she will have abundant milk and not cause him to die.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:14:4.hebrew: קורא - רך הגדל בדקל, מה שנוסף על הענף בשנה זו:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:14:4.english: Kora - A soft [shoot] that grows on a palm tree, that which is added onto the branch in this year.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:14:7.english: And harsana - Fish fried in flour and their brine and fat.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:14:8.hebrew: מינייהו פסקי חלבא - יש בדברים הללו שפוסקין חלב האשה, ויש בהן שאין מפסיקין אלא עוכרין:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:14:8.english: Some cause milk to dry up - Among these things, there are [some] that cause a woman's milk to dry up, and there are [some] among them that do not cause [it] to dry up, but rather spoil [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:1.english: Epileptic children - Children conceived there fall from an illness called pasion [epilepsy].

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:2.english: Shemutei - Long-necked, and it is a blemish.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:3.hebrew: גירדני - פי' אדם שנמרט שערות ראשו, או בעל גרב:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:3.english: Girddanei - Meaning: a person whose head hair has fallen out, or one afflicted with scurf [a skin disease].

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:5.english: Dulfanei - Their eyes drip water constantly.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:6.english: Moninei - She was accustomed to eating small fish.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:7.english: Blinking eyes - His eyes flutter and move constantly.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:15:8.hebrew: גרגושתא - אדמה, ארזילא"ה בלע"ז:

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:1:1.hebrew: עד עשרים וארבעה חדש - שמא תתעבר ותצטרך לגמול את בנה, ובעל זה אינו אביו שיקנה לו ביצים וחלב:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:1:1.english: Until twenty-four months - Lest she become pregnant and need to wean her son, and this [new] husband is not his father to buy him eggs and milk.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:1:2.english: Eighteen months - [That] is sufficient for an infant to nurse.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:5:2.english: That the matter will not succeed - that he will rule in accordance with the halakha.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:6:1.hebrew: נתנה בנה למינקת - זו שמת בעלה, או גמלתו בתוך זמנו, או מת:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:6:1.english: She gave her child to a wet nurse - This [refers to a woman] whose husband died, or [where] she weaned him within his [nursing] period, or he died.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:7:1.hebrew: לבי ריש גלותא - אלמנות שהיו בהן מניקות, ונתנו בניהם למניקה, והתירום לינשא:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:7:1.english: For the household of the Exilarch - Widows among them who were nursing, who gave their children to a wet nurse, and they permitted them to marry.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:7:2.hebrew: דלא הדרי בהו - מניקה שפסקה להניק בניהם יראה לחזור בה, לפי שבני אדם מאוימים הם. אבל באינשי אחריני, דלמא הדרא בה המניקה, וחוזר הבן אצל האם ומסתכן:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:7:2.english: For they do not renege - A wet nurse who contracted to nurse their children is afraid to retract, because they are feared people. However, with other people, perhaps the wet nurse will retract, and the child will return to the mother and be endangered.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:8:1.hebrew: לא תסברוה מהא - אי לא אמרה לכו סבתא משמי' דר"נ, לא הייתם יודעים ללמוד מתוך משנה זו שאסור:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:8:1.english: [Do you] not maintain it from this - If the old woman had not told you in the name of Rav Nachman, would you not have known to learn from this baraita [lit., mishnah] that it is prohibited?

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:8:2.hebrew: הרי שהיתה רדופה - רוב ימיה להיות בבית אביה כו'. כל אלו אין דרכן להתעבר:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:8:2.english: If she frequently [went] - [Spending] most of her days in her father’s house, etc. None of these [women] ordinarily conceive.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:8:3.english: [A woman] who is unfit to give birth - [One] whose womb was removed.

Rashi on Ketubot 60b:9:1.hebrew: בגזירותיו - בכל מקום שהוא מחמיר מדרבנן. אלמא, אע"ג דאין כאן להבחין בין זרעו של ראשון לשל שני — דהא לא מיעברא — לא פלוג רבנן בתקנת גזירות שלהם בין אשה לאשה, וגזרו סתם שתמתין כל אשה שלשה חדשים. והכי נמי לא פלוג רבנן במינקת שמת בעלה, בין שהיא מניקתו בין שאינה מניקתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 60b:9:1.english: With regard to his decrees - In every place where he is stringent by rabbinic decree. Thus [we see that] even though there is no [need] here to distinguish between the seed of the first [husband] and that of the second — for she cannot become pregnant — the Rabbis did not differentiate in the enactment of their decrees between one woman and another, and they decreed categorically that every woman must wait three months. So too, the Rabbis did not differentiate regarding a nursing woman whose husband died between [a case] where she is nursing him and [a case] where she is not nursing him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:10:1.hebrew: ואמר ר"נ אמר שמואל הלכה כר"מ בגזירותיו - אין לפרש דגזרינן מת אטו לא מת, ונתנה בנה להניק אטו לא נתנה, וגמלתו אטו לא גמלתו, דא"כ היכי שרא ר"נ לבי ריש גלותא? אלא י"ל דגזרינן במת שמא תהרגנו, ונתנה בנה להניק שמא תחזור בה, וגמלתו אטו שמא תגמלנו ועדיין הוא צריך לינק:
Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:10:1.english: And Rav Nachman said [that] Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir in his decrees - One should not explain that we decree [regarding a case where the child] died on account of [one where he] did not die, and [where] she gave her child to be nursed on account of [one where] she did not give [him], and [where] she weaned him on account of [one where] she did not wean him — for if so, how did Rav Nachman permit [it] for the house of the Exilarch? Rather, one can say that we decree in [a case where the child] died lest she kill him, and [where] she gave her child to be nursed lest she retract, and [where] she weaned him on account of [the concern] lest she wean him while he still needs to nurse.

Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:10:2.hebrew: והלכתא מת מותר גמלתו אסור - רבינו שמשון הזקן אומר דגרושה מותרת לינשא, דלא משעבדא להניק, כדתניא לעיל (כתובות דף נט:): "נתגרשה אינו כופה", משום דלא משעבדא לי'. ור"ת אומר דאסורה לינשא, דתניא בפ' החולץ (יבמות מב. ושם): "מעוברת חבירו ומינקת חבירו לא ישא", וקא פסיק ותני לא שנא נתאלמנה ולא שנא נתגרשה. ועוד, דמפרש טעמא התם דסתם מעוברת למניקה קיימא, דמשמע דהיינו טעמא דמניקה היינו טעמא דמעוברת; ולמאי דהוה מפרש מעיקרא, טעמא דמעוברת שייך בגרושה כמו באלמנה, אע"ג דהדר בי' מההוא טעמא — מגופא דמילתא לא הדר ביה, דמיירי אפי' בגרושה. ועוד, דאלמנה נמי לא משעבדא מכי תבעה כתובתה או רוצה לינשא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:10:2.english: And the halakha is: [If the child] died, it is permitted; [if] she weaned him, it is prohibited - Rabbeinu Shimshon the Elder says that a divorcee is permitted to marry [within twenty-four months], since she is not obligated to nurse, as it is taught in a baraita above (Ketubot 59b): "If she was divorced, he cannot compel her [to nurse]," because she is not obligated to him. But Rabbeinu Tam says that she is prohibited from marrying, for it is taught in a baraita in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 42a and there): "A man shall not marry another man's pregnant [wife] or another man's nursing [wife]," and [the Tanna] states categorically without distinguishing whether she was widowed or whether she was divorced. Furthermore, [the Gemara] explains the reason there that an ordinary pregnant woman stands to become a nursing woman, which implies that the reason for a nursing woman is the very same reason as for a pregnant woman; and according to what [the Gemara] initially explained, the reason for a pregnant woman applies to a divorcee just as to a widow, and even though [the Gemara] retracted that [initial] reason, it did not retract the substance of the matter itself — that [the baraita] refers even to a divorcee. And furthermore, a widow is also not obligated [to nurse] once she claims her ketubah or wishes to marry.

Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:5:1.hebrew: אפילו ביעתא בכותחא - מפרש בערוך, דלאו בסתם ביצים איירי, דאין לך עם הארץ שלא ידע שהן מותרות בחלב; אלא בשוחט תרנגולת ומצא בה ביצים גמורות מיירי, שמותר לאוכלן בחלב, כדתניא בפ"ק דביצה (דף ו: ושם). וא"ת: ואמאי מותר לאכלן בחלב, מאי שנא מביצת נבלה, דאסרי בית הלל אפי' כמוה נמכרת בשוק, כדתנן במסכת עדיות (פ"א מ"ה)? ותירץ בהלכות גדולות, דגבי איסור נבילה החמירו דהוי דאורייתא, אבל גבי בשר עוף בחלב דרבנן הקילו. וא"ת: ומאי אפי' דקאמר "אפילו ביעתא בכותחא", הא איכא מאן דאמר (חולין דף קיג.) בשר עוף בחלב דאורייתא, ולדידיה אסורה כמו ביצת נבילה? וי"ל: דמ"מ קאמר אפי', שכל העולם נהגו בו היתר. ולר"ת אתי שפיר, שתירץ דבביצת נבילה החמירו משום דנבלה דבר איסור הוא, אבל בבשר בחלב לא החמירו דהוי היתר, דכל חד וחד באפי נפשיה שרי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:5:1.english: Even an egg in kutach - The Arukh explains that it is not speaking of ordinary eggs, for there is no ignoramus who does not know that they are permitted with milk; rather, it is speaking of one who slaughters a hen and finds fully formed eggs inside it, which are permitted to be eaten with milk, as is taught in a baraita in the first chapter of Beitzah (6b and there [in the Gemara]). And if you ask: Why is it permitted to eat them with milk — how is it different from an egg of a nevelah [an unslaughtered carcass], which Beit Hillel prohibit even when its like is sold in the market, as we learned in the Mishnah in Tractate Eduyot (1:5)? And it is answered in Halakhot Gedolot that regarding the prohibition of nevelah they were stringent because it is biblical, whereas regarding fowl meat in milk, which is rabbinic, they were lenient. And if you ask: What is [the meaning of] "even" that he says [in] "even an egg in kutach" — behold, there is an authority who says (Chullin 113a) [that] fowl meat in milk is biblical, and according to him it would be prohibited just like the egg of a nevelah? One can answer: Nevertheless he says "even," since the entire world treats it as permitted. And according to Rabbeinu Tam it works out well, for he answered that regarding an egg of a nevelah they were stringent because a nevelah is an inherently prohibited thing, whereas regarding meat in milk they were not stringent because it is [composed of] permitted [items], as each one by itself is permitted.

Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:5:2.hebrew: כי אפקירותא - ונפקא מיניה, שהיכא שהרב מוחל על כבודו דשרי — ואפ"ה אל יורה, דלא מסתייע מילתא הואיל ורבו אצלו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:5:2.english: "Like disrespect" - And the practical difference [between the two reasons] is that where the teacher waives his honor, where it is [otherwise] permitted — even so, one should not rule, because the matter will not succeed since his teacher is with him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:9:1.hebrew: ואמר ר"נ אמר שמואל הלכה כר"מ בגזירותיו - אין לפרש דגזרינן מת אטו לא מת, ונתנה בנה להניק אטו לא נתנה, וגמלתו אטו לא גמלתו; דא"כ, היכי שרא ר"נ לבי ריש גלותא? אלא י"ל דגזרינן: במת — שמא תהרגנו, ונתנה בנה להניק — שמא תחזור בה, וגמלתו — אטו שמא תגמלנו ועדיין הוא צריך לינק:
Tosafot on Ketubot 60b:9:1.english: And Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir with regard to his decrees - One should not explain that we decree [regarding a woman whose child] died on account of [one whose child] did not die, and [regarding a woman who] gave her child to be nursed on account of [one who] did not give [him], and [regarding a woman who] weaned him on account of [one who] did not wean him; for if so, how did Rav Nachman permit [it] for the household of the Exilarch? Rather, one must say that we decree: regarding [a woman whose child] died — lest she kill him; and [regarding a woman who] gave her child to be nursed — lest she [the wet nurse] retract; and [regarding a woman who] weaned him — lest she wean him while he still needs to nurse.
